dlg.vonnra.fortune.2.intent: to read the result of her own work
dlg.vonnra.fortune.2.wants: to read the result of her own work
dlg.vonnra.fortune.2.note: Commands, unhurried. 'No, the other one' precise. 'I have been waiting to see how it came out.' the only hint of appetite in her voice. 'No charge, this once.' is the call's twin (C01): the same phrasing, close and quiet across a table, so a listener can find it.

dlg.vonnra.f_ember.5.intent: to warn that the trade will finish itself
dlg.vonnra.f_ember.5.wants: to see whether you will be the one who stops them
dlg.vonnra.f_ember.5.note: 'Someone always does' is a law she lives by. Neither threat nor regret; a ledger fact.
dlg.vonnra.f_ember.5.hides: she let the caravan be taken so these crates would never reach the Dig

dlg.vonnra.f_ember.6.intent: to plant a question they have not asked
dlg.vonnra.f_ember.6.wants: to see whether you will be the one who stops them
dlg.vonnra.f_ember.6.note: She knows what B.E. means and lets the letters hang unread. 'Someone always does' is quiet and certain.
dlg.vonnra.f_ember.6.hides: she let the caravan be taken so these crates would never reach the Dig

dlg.sella.morning.3.intent: to send them off without admitting she cares
dlg.sella.morning.3.wants: to send them off without admitting she cares
dlg.sella.morning.3.note: Morning-after banter, frank and funny. 'The pieces are what I like' is bawdy and also a real wish for them to come back alive.

dlg.sella.past.4.note: She listens properly and enjoys the picture of them young. 'I'd have guessed, but not that' is warm and slightly puzzled. What is said here may be sold, and she knows it.

dlg.sella.past.5.note: A gentle tease ('cloister rat'), then 'Good for you, love' warmly meant: she knows about getting out.

dlg.sella.past.6.note: The pause is her low laugh. 'Takes one to know one' hints at her own past, unexplained. 'Don't tell Rook' is a shared joke.

dlg.sella.past.7.intent: to honour what they told her
dlg.sella.past.7.wants: to honour what they told her
dlg.sella.past.7.note: She is quiet a moment before the second sentence. 'Saddest thing' is said without performance; the last clause keeps it from tipping into pity.

dlg.snib.first.1.intent: to stop the intruder and look important
dlg.snib.first.1.wants: to stop the intruder and look important
dlg.snib.first.1.note: Big shout on 'OI!', a lamp-ring on the stressed words. Then the self-introduction is proud and small. 'It does, actually' is the contradiction gag: a sudden honest deflation before 'But quick'.

dlg.snib.hub.1.intent: to sound in charge of a change he fears
dlg.snib.hub.1.wants: to sound in charge of a change he fears
dlg.snib.hub.1.note: 'Boss likes deeper' is brave; 'Boss has not SAID he likes it' is the panic underneath. Settle back into 'Foreman is still foreman' as reassurance to himself.

dlg.snib.hub.2.intent: to show nothing has changed and he is in charge
dlg.snib.hub.2.wants: to show nothing has changed and he is in charge
dlg.snib.hub.2.note: Weary self-important routine, two status reports.

say.48cdd82e6c0b.intent: to make the player feel one charge's weight in the hand
say.48cdd82e6c0b.wants: to make the player feel one charge's weight in the hand
say.48cdd82e6c0b.note: Low and close, as if not to wake them. A pause before 'the way they have waited for everyone'.

say.4acad56ca838.intent: to let the relief arrive in the silence
say.4acad56ca838.wants: to let the relief arrive in the silence
say.4acad56ca838.note: 'One at a time' slow; 'not go off' flat and quiet.
